title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'spaces' (tame or polyhedral) without points. The data are a set M of 'figures' with two relations. X ≤ Y is containment. X ≪ Y is a weaker relation, roughly 'X is in the shadow of Y'. omb(X) is the 'shadow' (ombre) of X, the set of minimal elements below X for ≪. ≪° is an 'interior' variant. On p.51 he listed two possible axiom systems. Version (1), 'Prat 1-6', uses a compatibility relation ≬ on all of M. Version (2), 'Prat Λ', adds a dense subset Λ ⊂ M. On this page he gives a third conception (③), meant for polyhedral structures. Compatibility ≬ on M is no longer primitive. Instead it is replaced by a 'disjunction' relation ‖ defined only on L, the set of minimal elements of (M, ≪), i.e. the 'lieux' or generalized points (cf. p.34).

The axioms Prat dis 1'-4' are Prat Λ 1-4 with Λ = L:
- (1') X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y.
- (2') Density: every X has a point x ∈ L with x ≪° X, i.e. omb(X)° ≠ ∅.
- (3') Small neighbourhoods: if x ≪ X, there is X' ∈ M with x ≪° X' ≤ X.
- (4') Shadow of an intersection: take Y ≪ X and X' ≤ X, and a point x with x ≪ Y and x ≪ X'. Then there is Y' ≤ Y with Y' ≪ X' and x ≪ Y'. Equivalently omb(Y) ∩ omb(X') = omb(Y_{X'}), where Y_{X'} = Ỹ ∩ omb(X'). Here Ỹ is the down-set of figures ≤ Y, and the shadow of a set is the union of the shadows of its members. If moreover Y ≤ X, one may take Y' ≤ X' (the image has X, probably a slip), giving omb(Y) ∩ omb(X') = omb(Ỹ ∩ X̃').

The last two axioms involve ‖:
- (5') ‖ is symmetric and antireflexive. This is simpler than the old Prat Λ 5.
- (6') If Y ≤ X, y ∈ omb(Y) and x ∈ omb(X) \ omb(Y), then x ‖ y. Points of a figure lying outside a subfigure are 'disjoint' from the points of that subfigure.

Compatibility is then defined: X ≬ Y iff, with L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ, every x ∈ omb(X) \ omb(L) is disjoint (‖) from every y ∈ omb(Y) \ omb(L). In the polyhedral case one also requires L = ∅ or L = Z̃ for a single figure Z. That is the familiar 'two cells meet in a common face or not at all' condition of polyhedral or regular cell complexes.

The next page adds 'Prat pol' (local existence of meets). It also checks the simplicial-complex example, with ≪ = ≤ and x ‖ y ⇔ x ≠ y: all axioms hold except 'divisibility'.

Purpose: to reduce the compatibility structure on figures to a binary 'separation' relation on minimal figures (points/lieux). This is a step toward a pointless, combinatorial axiomatization of tame and polyhedral topology, in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Prat dis 4', 'De plus, si Y ≤ X, OPS Y' ≤ X': by analogy with Prat Λ 4 on p.51 ('Si Y ≤ X, alors Y' ≤ X'') this should read Y' ≤ X'. As written it is trivial.
Notation clash: L denotes both the set of minimal elements of (M, ≪) and the down-set X̃ ∩ Ỹ (or Ỹ ∩ X̃') in Prat dis 4' and in the definition of ≬.
omb is applied both to figures and to down-sets (omb(L) := union of omb(Z), Z ∈ L). This is only made explicit once, in Prat dis 4'.

Unproved at this stage: that the defined ≬ satisfies the old compatibility axioms. In particular the analogue of Prat Λ 5 (shadow of compatible figures is the shadow of their meet) needs the polyhedral clause L = Z̃ plus Prat dis 4'. The page asserts the equivalence of conceptions only implicitly.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a space via a poset of 'figures' with a containment order ≤ and a weaker 'shadow' relation ≪, with points recovered as minimal elements (lieux)
ideas.modern_name: pointless topology / cellular and stratified posets; closest are face posets of CW/polyhedral complexes and Alexandrov-type finite spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone); face-poset combinatorics (Björner et al.); Grothendieck's tame topology programme in outline
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic 'topologie modérée' section of Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axiomatics itself is unpublished

ideas.what: Replacing a compatibility relation on all figures by a symmetric antireflexive 'disjunction' relation ‖ on minimal elements, with compatibility defined from it
ideas.modern_name: apartness/separation relation on points; proper intersection of cells
ideas.usually_credited_to: apartness relations in constructive analysis (Brouwer, Heyting); no direct analogue in tame topology

ideas.what: Polyhedral condition: two compatible figures meet in a single figure or not at all (X̃ ∩ Ỹ empty or principal)
ideas.modern_name: intersection property of polyhedral / regular CW complexes; meet-semilattice of faces

ideas.what: Shadow-of-intersection axiom omb(Y) ∩ omb(X') = omb(Ỹ ∩ omb(X'))
ideas.modern_name: locality / intersection axiom for a basis of a topology

missed.claim: A third, 'disjunction-based' axiomatization of polyhedral spaces via (M, ≤, ≪, ‖ on minimal elements), with compatibility derived. Its equivalence with the Prat Λ system and its sufficiency for polyhedra are left unproved. The margin itself flags the 'true' axiomatization problem for polyhedral structures as harder.
missed.quote: ③ Cas des structures spaciales polyédrales, exprimées en termes de (M, ≤, ≪, ‖_L), où ‖_L est une relation "de disjonction" sur L = ens. des él. minim. de (M, ≪)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A purely order-theoretic characterization of polyhedral or tame spaces by a poset of closed pieces plus a separation relation on minimal pieces could inform combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path posets, conically smooth structures) and definable cell decompositions. No such axiomatization from Grothendieck is in the literature, but the page is a sketch, not a result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a mid-stream working variant of an unpublished axiomatics for tame/polyhedral topology. It is interesting as evidence of how Grothendieck tried to realize the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée'. The individual axioms are elementary and close to standard properties of cell complexes. Nothing finished or striking beyond the existence of the programme itself.
transcription_corrections: The defined relation at the bottom is the compatibility symbol: 'X ≬ Y ⟺ ...', not 'X Λ Y'.
Prat dis 4' is written as a vertical diagram: 'Y ≪ X' with 'X'' below X joined by a rotated ≤ (i.e. X' ≤ X).
Prat dis 4', 'De plus, si Y ≤ X, OPS Y' ≤ X': OPS = 'on peut supposer'; mathematically X' is intended.
Bracketed remark after Prat dis 6': 'Seules les deux dernières axiomes font intervenir ‖'.
Left margin at top: 'dis pour "disjonction"' and a gloss on 'Prat'; the second word is uncertain.
